messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target
      # resources (a hard build input). The real plist is gitignored; the
      # release path writes it from GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1656
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1656
- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +267
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T23:24:47Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

blocks.text:
# pr-1656: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

- **Title**: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1655` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +267
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-16T14:03:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-16T23:24:47Z

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

blocks.text:
The Android app uses `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion` — i.e., whatever NDK Flutter's tool config declares. On the CI, Flutter stable 3.47.7 was used, and Gradle requested NDK 28.2.13676358 (android-ndk-r28c). The sdkmanager download got corrupted at 33% — that's a transient network/storage error on the runner, not a code defect.

But wait — is it really transient? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%: the download jumped from 19% to 33% then immediately "Unzipping..." — this suggests the download actually FAILED fast and sdkmanager tried to unzip an incomplete file. That's classic transient network flake (connection cut mid-download → truncated archive).

Key question: is this deterministic on this runner image (20261012.334)? Let me check the history of the build-android leg on this PR and on main:

1. Did build-android succeed on other commits in this PR? The PR had previous runs (red 1/3, red 2/3 notices — those were the two reds mentioned; both on head 96d3a8f... wait no, the notices say "red head 96d3a8f" twice, red 1/3 and red 2/3 — actually the general comments say red head 96d3a8f 1/3 and 2/3 — hmm, but there's also mention of head d99b764 (cancelled) and rework on 96d3a8f).

Let me check run history for the build-mobile workflow to see if build-android succeeded recently on main, and on the PR's earlier heads. If build-android succeeded on main recently with the same runner image, then this is a flake and a re-run would fix it. If it's been failing since the runner image changed (20261012.334), then we need a real fix — e.g., pre-install NDK via sdkmanager with retries in the workflow, or accept a signed license + retry.

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1

          distribution: 'temurin'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=

blocks.text:
# pr-1656: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

The Android app uses `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion` — i.e., whatever NDK Flutter's tool config declares. On the CI, Flutter stable 3.47.7 was used, and Gradle requested NDK 28.2.13676358 (android-ndk-r28c). The sdkmanager download got corrupted at 33% — that's a transient network/storage error on the runner, not a code defect.

But wait — is it really transient? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%: the download jumped from 19% to 33% then immediately "Unzipping..." — this suggests the download actually FAILED fast and sdkmanager tried to unzip an incomplete file. That's classic transient network flake (connection cut mid-download → truncated archive).

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }

# pr-1656: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset

          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target

blocks.text:
# pr-1656: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

The Android app uses `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion` — i.e., whatever NDK Flutter's tool config declares. On the CI, Flutter stable 3.47.7 was used, and Gradle requested NDK 28.2.13676358 (android-ndk-r28c). The sdkmanager download got corrupted at 33% — that's a transient network/storage error on the runner, not a code defect.

But wait — is it really transient? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%: the download jumped from 19% to 33% then immediately "Unzipping..." — this suggests the download actually FAILED fast and sdkmanager tried to unzip an incomplete file. That's classic transient network flake (connection cut mid-download → truncated archive).

Key question: is this deterministic on this runner image (20261012.334)? Let me check the history of the build-android leg on this PR and on main:

1. Did build-android succeed on other commits in this PR? The PR had previous runs (red 1/3, red 2/3 notices — those were the two reds mentioned; both on head 96d3a8f... wait no, the notices say "red head 96d3a8f" twice, red 1/3 and red 2/3 — actually the general comments say red head 96d3a8f 1/3 and 2/3 — hmm, but there's also mention of head d99b764 (cancelled) and rework on 96d3a8f).

Let me check run history for the build-mobile workflow to see if build-android succeeded recently on main, and on the PR's earlier heads. If build-android succeeded on main recently with the same runner image, then this is a flake and a re-run would fix it. If it's been failing since the runner image changed (20261012.334), then we need a real fix — e.g., pre-install NDK via sdkmanager with retries in the workflow, or accept a signed license + retry.

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:

# pr-1656: gh-1655 [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

On the CI, Flutter stable 3.47.7 was used, and Gradle requested NDK 28.2.13676358 (android-ndk-r28c). The sdkmanager download got corrupted at 33% — that's a transient network/storage error on the runner, not a code defect.

But wait — is it really transient? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%: the download jumped from 19% to 33% then immediately "Unzipping..." — this suggests the download actually FAILED fast and sdkmanager tried to unzip an incomplete file. That's classic transient network flake (connection cut mid-download → truncated archive).

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target
      # resources (a hard build input). The real plist is gitignored; the

messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

The Android app uses `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion` — i.e., whatever NDK Flutter's tool config declares. On the CI, Flutter stable 3.47.7 was used, and Gradle requested NDK 28.2.13676358 (android-ndk-r28c). The sdkmanager download got corrupted at 33% — that's a transient network/storage error on the runner, not a code defect.

But wait — is it really transient? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%: the download jumped from 19% to 33% then immediately "Unzipping..." — this suggests the download actually FAILED fast and sdkmanager tried to unzip an incomplete file. That's classic transient network flake (connection cut mid-download → truncated archive).

Key question: is this deterministic on this runner image (20261012.334)? Let me check the history of the build-android leg on this PR and on main:

1. Did build-android succeed on other commits in this PR? The PR had previous runs (red 1/3, red 2/3 notices — those were the two reds mentioned; both on head 96d3a8f... wait no, the notices say "red head 96d3a8f" twice, red 1/3 and red 2/3 — actually the general comments say red head 96d3a8f 1/3 and 2/3 — hmm, but there's also mention of head d99b764 (cancelled) and rework on 96d3a8f).

Let me check run history for the build-mobile workflow to see if build-android succeeded recently on main, and on the PR's earlier heads. If build-android succeeded on main recently with the same runner image, then this is a flake and a re-run would fix it. If it's been failing since the runner image changed (20261012.334), then we need a real fix — e.g., pre-install NDK via sdkmanager with retries in the workflow, or accept a signed license + retry.

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target
      # resources (a hard build input). The real plist is gitignored; the
      # release path writes it from GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64

messages.preview: The Android build failed during NDK auto-install: `Error on ZipFile unknown archive` — the NDK 28.2.13676358 download came back truncated/corrupt. Let me look at how the NDK is requested and whether t…

blocks.text:
Interesting. The Android build failed because:

```
Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358: Error on ZipFile unknown archive.
```

The NDK download was truncated at 33% — "Error on ZipFile unknown archive". This looks like an infra/network failure on the runner, NOT a code failure. The Gradle build at `flutter_app/android/build.gradle.kts` line 73 invokes sdkmanager to install the NDK, and the download was corrupted/truncated.

Let me check the beginning of the log to see the workflow steps and whether previous runs of this build leg succeeded on this same commit. Let me also check the build.gradle.kts line 73 and whether the NDK version pinned matches an available one.

Key question: is this a flaky infra failure (partial download), or is the pinned NDK version invalid (e.g., removed from Google's repository)? "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" is the classic symptom of a truncated/corrupt download OR of a requested NDK version whose archive URL 404s (sdkmanager writes an HTML error page to the zip). If the NDK version is removed/invalid, sdkmanager reports "Error: The following Android SDK packages were not found" or similar; if it 404s mid-download, "Error on ZipFile" can appear.

Let me look at the full log to see how the NDK got requested. Line 73 of build.gradle.kts. Let me check the workflow definition for build-mobile.yml.

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target
