name: flutter-gemma-android-seed
description: >-
  Pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android native cache so the
  flutter_gemma_litertlm build hook never downloads
  litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build. gh-1468: one HTTP 500 from the
  github.com release-asset CDN during that download red'd the ci.yml
  build-android leg (and the aggregate Quality gate with it). The hook
  short-circuits the download entirely once libLiteRtLm.so and a matching
  .flutter_gemma_native_version marker exist in the cache — same
  hardening the macOS legs carry via "Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion
  dylibs". The version/checksum below MUST equal the hook's _litertlmBundle
  registration in the pinned flutter_gemma_litertlm (hook/build.dart);
  test/ci_gemma_android_seed_guard_test.dart AC3 cross-checks both sides.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Seed flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/.cache/flutter_gemma/native"
        PLATFORM_DIR="$GEMMA_CACHE/android_arm64"
        MARKER="$GEMMA_CACHE/.flutter_gemma_native_version"
        # The hook's cache-dedup predicate: main lib present AND the
        # marker carries this bundle's exact version (its
        # _invalidateBundleCacheIfStale wipes owned files on a version
        # mismatch, so a stale seed would be deleted and re-downloaded
        # mid-build — the roulette this action exists to stop).
        if [ -f "$PLATFORM_DIR/libLiteRtLm.so" ] && \
           grep -q '"version":"0.17.1-a"\|"version": *"0.17.1-a"' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs already cached ($PLATFORM_DIR)"
        else
          echo "seeding flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs from native-v0.17.1-a"
          mkdir -p "$PLATFORM_DIR"
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.17.1-a/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz
          echo "745b89b606eb712a78f06aed41daca1370eae79b00e0a36054c8e775c0251768  /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz -C "$PLATFORM_DIR"
          # Marker commit point: {version, owner} exactly as the hook's
          # _writeMarker emits it (owner = the hook's _packageName) so the
          # pre-seeded cache keeps a single CodeAsset registrant.
          printf '{"version":"0.17.1-a","owner":"flutter_gemma_litertlm"}\n' > "$MARKER"
        fi
        ls -la "$PLATFORM_DIR"

build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON secret is not set — the Play Developer API service-account JSON key is required"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          echo "All required Android secrets are present"

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@e81a8fa391b11a595c1b7ed84177cc0fe02faf83 # v1.328.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # gh-1468: same seed as ci.yml build-android — the release lane runs
      # the same flutter_gemma_litertlm hook download and rides the same
      # release-asset CDN roulette without it.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

          # placeholder and never churns. BUILD_NUMBER stays the run number
          # (Play versionCode).
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}

    # GitHub release. store keeps its AAB for Play and additionally gets

      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # Same placeholder-.env incantation as build-android (issue #368):
      # .env is a declared Flutter asset and newer flutter validates
      # assets at build time.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors build-android, gated to the store flavor: the secret file
      # carries ONLY the dev.fa1.app client, while the god applicationId is
      # dev.fa1.app.god — overwriting it would hard-fail the google-services

      # 'dev.fa1.app.god'"). god builds with the committed placeholder

      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ "$FLAVOR" != "store" ]; then
            echo "$FLAVOR builds with the committed placeholder google-services.json — the secret file has no dev.fa1.app.god client"

            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written"
          else

Fixing build-mobile.yml too follows "check same pattern across codebase" and is cheap/reusable. gh-1468's seed was applied to both ci.yml and build-mobile.yml with the same reasoning ("same hardening as the release lane rides the same roulette"). I'll follow that precedent.

Also — do I need to check `sdkmanager` availability? On ubuntu-latest runner images, `$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager` exists. Gradle's log shows it invoked `/usr/local/lib/android/sdk/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager`. So sdkmanager is available at `$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager`.

`yes | sdkmanager --install ...` — for license acceptance. The licenses were already accepted in the failing run (the download started without a license prompt), but including `--licenses` acceptance is safer... Actually the build-android job on this image already auto-installs the NDK from gradle without a license issue, so licenses are pre-accepted. I'll still use `yes | sdkmanager` to be robust.

About idempotence check: check if `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/$NDK_VERSION` already exists → skip. Also skip downloading when present mid-way? A partially-installed dir from a previous failed attempt: sdkmanager cleans up on failure (it unzips to temp first), but to be safe the retry loop can `rm -rf` the target dir before each attempt.

Also important: Gradle config resolved the NDK via the sdkmanager because the NDK wasn't installed. Once pre-installed at `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/28.2.13676358`, AGP finds it and skips the download entirely (that's the point).

description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated NDK download ("Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%) red'd
  the ci.yml build-android leg and the aggregate Quality gate with it;
  Gradle's own auto-install path has no retry. The NDK version is resolved
  from the pinned Flutter SDK's gradle plugin source (the exact value
  flutter.ndkVersion resolves to — no second pin to drift), the install is
  skipped when the NDK is already present, and the download itself is
  bounded-retried — the same hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed
  carries (gh-1468).
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at config
        # time (a literal pin on either side would break that coupling —
        # the ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test pins both sides).
        FLUTTER_HOME="${FLUTTER_ROOT:-$(dirname "$(dirname "$(command -v flutter)")}"
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall"
          exit 1
        fi
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager)"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call, run
        # inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — the download-roulette gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1
```

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e added GoogleService-Info.plist to the Runner target
      # resources (a hard build input). The real plist is gitignored; the
      # release path writes it from GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64

Confirmed: **the same NDK download (`android-ndk-r28c-linux`) succeeded 4 minutes later on main's run** (22:32:34 → completed, build went green). The PR run's NDK download was truncated at 33% ("Error on ZipFile unknown archive"). This is a transient network flake on the runner — the NDK download dies mid-stream and sdkmanager unzips a truncated archive.

However — a purely flaky failure still reddened the required Quality gate twice (red 1/3, red 2/3 on the same head; a third red escalates to a human). The rework pass is expected to fix the CI root cause. Two options:

1. **Just re-run** — but I can't re-run CI from here reliably (and instructions say fix the root cause in code/config).
2. **Harden the workflow** so a truncated NDK download doesn't fail the build — e.g., pre-install the NDK before Gradle runs (with retry), so Gradle config never triggers a mid-build sdkmanager download that can't be retried.

The PR diff didn't touch the workflow or Android config, so this failure is NOT caused by the PR code. But the machine threads require the head to go green. The rework contract: "Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup."

The right hardening: in ci.yml's build-android job (and build-mobile.yml's Android jobs?), pre-install the pinned NDK with a retried download before `flutter build apk`. - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-${{ steps.week.outputs.epoch }}
          restore-keys: |
            ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git (the release path
          # prefers the self-hosted runner's local copy; GitHub-hosted PR
          # legs always take the pinned upstream fallback).
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56).
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
            https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)
        # E2, corrected by gh-1296: classify the failure by EVIDENCE in the
        # log, not by a blanket keyword. The old grep matched 'cocoapods' or
        # 'pod install' in EVERY flutter iOS build log ("Running pod
        # install… 4.4s" prints even on green builds), so every failure was
        # mislabeled "CocoaPods layer — likely spec drift" — that
        # mislabeling sent gh-1296 at a Podfile.lock fix while the real
        # killer was a package build hook (sqlite3's native-assets download
        # hash check). Most-specific layer first; unmatched failures stay
        # unlabeled rather than guessed.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          cd flutter_app
          if ! flutter build ios --debug --no-codesign 2>&1 | tee /tmp/build-ios.log; then
            if grep -qE 'Building native assets failed|build_hooks failed|Hash of downloaded file|build\.dart returned with exit code' /tmp/build-ios.log; then
              if grep -q 'Hash of downloaded file' /tmp/build-ios.log; then
                echo "::error::iOS build failed in the NATIVE-ASSETS layer: a package build hook downloaded a prebuilt artifact whose SHA-256 no longer matches the hash pinned in the package (upstream re-uploaded a release asset, gh-1296). NOT a CocoaPods/Podfile problem. It self-heals when upstream restores the asset — or bump the package version. The hook's 'To reproduce run:' line above names the package; check its GitHub releases. Raw log above."
              else
                echo "::error::iOS build failed in the NATIVE-ASSETS layer: a package build hook (hook/build.dart) failed. The log names the package and its 'To reproduce run:' line — reproduce locally. NOT a CocoaPods/Podfile problem. Raw log above."
              fi
            elif grep -qE "CocoaPods could not find compatible versions|The sandbox is not in sync with the Podfile\.lock|No podspec found|Error running pod install|Unable to satisfy the following requirements" /tmp/build-ios.log; then
              echo "::error::iOS build failed in the CocoaPods layer — spec/sandbox drift. Fix: cd flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update, commit the regenerated Podfile.lock (the pods cache re-rolls weekly, see the cache step; scripts/check_lockfiles.sh pod-sync catches this class pre-merge). Raw log above."
            else
              echo "::error::iOS build failed (Xcode/app layer — no CocoaPods or native-assets signature in the log; read the first error above)."
            fi
            exit 1
          fi

messages.preview: The repo has an established hardening precedent (gh-1468: pre-seed external downloads so Gradle never fetches mid-build unretryably). The right fix: **pre-install the Flutter-pinned NDK with retries**…

blocks.text:
The repo has established patterns:
1. Pre-seeding external downloads before a build (gh-1468 flutter-gemma-android-seed) — "one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate Quality gate".
2. Retry-with-evidence pattern for transient mid-transfer failures (curl --retry, gh-1412 one-shot retry).

So the established fix for the Android leg: **pre-install the NDK (with retry) before `flutter build apk`**, so Gradle config never triggers an unretryable mid-build sdkmanager download. This exactly matches the gh-1468 pattern ("same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step").

name: flutter-gemma-android-seed
description: >-
  Pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android native cache so the
  flutter_gemma_litertlm build hook never downloads
  litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build. gh-1468: one HTTP 500 from the
  github.com release-asset CDN during that download red'd the ci.yml
  build-android leg (and the aggregate Quality gate with it). The hook
  short-circuits the download entirely once libLiteRtLm.so and a matching
  .flutter_gemma_native_version marker exist in the cache — same
  hardening the macOS legs carry via "Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion
  dylibs". The version/checksum below MUST equal the hook's _litertlmBundle
  registration in the pinned flutter_gemma_litertlm (hook/build.dart);
  test/ci_gemma_android_seed_guard_test.dart AC3 cross-checks both sides.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Seed flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/.cache/flutter_gemma/native"
        PLATFORM_DIR="$GEMMA_CACHE/android_arm64"
        MARKER="$GEMMA_CACHE/.flutter_gemma_native_version"
        # The hook's cache-dedup predicate: main lib present AND the
        # marker carries this bundle's exact version (its
        # _invalidateBundleCacheIfStale wipes owned files on a version
        # mismatch, so a stale seed would be deleted and re-downloaded
        # mid-build — the roulette this action exists to stop).
        if [ -f "$PLATFORM_DIR/libLiteRtLm.so" ] && \
           grep -q '"version":"0.17.1-a"\|"version": *"0.17.1-a"' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs already cached ($PLATFORM_DIR)"
        else
          echo "seeding flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs from native-v0.17.1-a"
          mkdir -p "$PLATFORM_DIR"
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.17.1-a/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz
          echo "745b89b606eb712a78f06aed41daca1370eae79b00e0a36054c8e775c0251768  /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz -C "$PLATFORM_DIR"
          # Marker commit point: {version, owner} exactly as the hook's
          # _writeMarker emits it (owner = the hook's _packageName) so the
          # pre-seeded cache keeps a single CodeAsset registrant.
          printf '{"version":"0.17.1-a","owner":"flutter_gemma_litertlm"}\n' > "$MARKER"
        fi
        ls -la "$PLATFORM_DIR"

build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON secret is not set — the Play Developer API service-account JSON key is required"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          echo "All required Android secrets are present"

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.

    # GitHub release. store keeps its AAB for Play and additionally gets
    # an APK for direct installs + the UT-CI-1 size-delta tracking.
    name: Build Android APK (${{ matrix.flavor }})
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1

          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # Same placeholder-.env incantation as build-android (issue #368):
      # .env is a declared Flutter asset and newer flutter validates
      # assets at build time.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors build-android, gated to the store flavor: the secret file
      # carries ONLY the dev.fa1.app client, while the god applicationId is
      # dev.fa1.app.god — overwriting it would hard-fail the google-services
      # plugin ("No matching client found for package name
      # 'dev.fa1.app.god'"). god builds with the committed placeholder
      # google-services.json, which carries both clients.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ "$FLAVOR" != "store" ]; then
            echo "$FLAVOR builds with the committed placeholder google-services.json — the secret file has no dev.fa1.app.god client"
          elif [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written"
          else
            echo "GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"

        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so

- name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-${{ steps.week.outputs.epoch }}
          restore-keys: |
            ios-pods-ci-v1-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}-

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git (the release path
          # prefers the self-hosted runner's local copy; GitHub-hosted PR
          # legs always take the pinned upstream fallback).
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56).
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
            https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)
        # E2, corrected by gh-1296: classify the failure by EVIDENCE in the
        # log, not by a blanket keyword. The old grep matched 'cocoapods' or
        # 'pod install' in EVERY flutter iOS build log ("Running pod
        # install… 4.4s" prints even on green builds), so every failure was
        # mislabeled "CocoaPods layer — likely spec drift" — that
        # mislabeling sent gh-1296 at a Podfile.lock fix while the real
        # killer was a package build hook (sqlite3's native-assets download
        # hash check). Most-specific layer first; unmatched failures stay
        # unlabeled rather than guessed.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          cd flutter_app
          if ! flutter build ios --debug --no-codesign 2>&1 | tee /tmp/build-ios.log; then
            if grep -qE 'Building native assets failed|build_hooks failed|Hash of downloaded file|build\.dart returned with exit code' /tmp/build-ios.log; then
              if grep -q 'Hash of downloaded file' /tmp/build-ios.log; then
                echo "::error::iOS build failed in the NATIVE-ASSETS layer: a package build hook downloaded a prebuilt artifact whose SHA-256 no longer matches the hash pinned in the package (upstream re-uploaded a release asset, gh-1296). NOT a CocoaPods/Podfile problem. It self-heals when upstream restores the asset — or bump the package version. The hook's 'To reproduce run:' line above names the package; check its GitHub releases. Raw log above."
              else
                echo "::error::iOS build failed in the NATIVE-ASSETS layer: a package build hook (hook/build.dart) failed. The log names the package and its 'To reproduce run:' line — reproduce locally. NOT a CocoaPods/Podfile problem. Raw log above."
              fi
            elif grep -qE "CocoaPods could not find compatible versions|The sandbox is not in sync with the Podfile\.lock|No podspec found|Error running pod install|Unable to satisfy the following requirements" /tmp/build-ios.log; then
              echo "::error::iOS build failed in the CocoaPods layer — spec/sandbox drift. Fix: cd flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update, commit the regenerated Podfile.lock (the pods cache re-rolls weekly, see the cache step; scripts/check_lockfiles.sh pod-sync catches this class pre-merge). Raw log above."
            else
              echo "::error::iOS build failed (Xcode/app layer — no CocoaPods or native-assets signature in the log; read the first error above)."
            fi
            exit 1
          fi

messages.preview: The repo has an established hardening precedent (gh-1468: pre-seed external downloads so Gradle never fetches mid-build unretryably). The right fix: **pre-install the Flutter-pinned NDK with retries**…

blocks.text:
The repo has established patterns:
1. Pre-seeding external downloads before a build (gh-1468 flutter-gemma-android-seed) — "one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate Quality gate".
2. Retry-with-evidence pattern for transient mid-transfer failures (curl --retry, gh-1412 one-shot retry).

So the established fix for the Android leg: **pre-install the NDK (with retry) before `flutter build apk`**, so Gradle config never triggers an unretryable mid-build sdkmanager download. This exactly matches the gh-1468 pattern ("same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step").

Which NDK version? `flutter.ndkVersion` for Flutter 3.47.x — the failing run requested **NDK (Side by side) 28.2.13676358** (android-ndk-r28c). Pinning a literal in the workflow risks drift with `flutter.ndkVersion` when Flutter bumps. Better: resolve `flutter.ndkVersion` at runtime:

```bash
NDK_VERSION=$(cd flutter_app && flutter config --list 2>/dev/null | ...)
```

Hmm, how to resolve flutter.ndkVersion reliably? Options:

1. `grep ndkVersion $FLUTTER_ROOT/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension... ` — fragile.
2. Pre-install via sdkmanager the exact version and retry: `sdkmanager --install "ndk;28.2.13676358"` — version hard-coded, drifts when Flutter updates.
3. A robust runtime resolution: use gradle to print it? Too heavy.

Actually there's a canonical way to read the Flutter default NDK version:

```bash
cat "$FLUTTER_ROOT/bin/cache/flutter_tools.snapshot" # binary, no
```

The flutter gradle plugin defines ndkVersion in `flutter/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt`? Actually in recent Flutter it's `FlutterExtension.Companion.ndkVersion = "28.2.13676358"`? Let me think — in Flutter repo, `packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/groovy/flutter.groovy` or `FlutterExtension.groovy` has `ndkVersion`. Hmm, but on the CI runner, $FLUTTER_ROOT is the flutter SDK — we can grep for the version string there:

```bash
NDK="$(grep -rhoE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' --include='*.kt' --include='*.groovy' "$FLUTTER_ROOT/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/" | grep ...)" 
```

too fragile. Alternative robust approach: derive from `flutter build` failure? No.

Alternative approach — instead of pre-installing a version, make Gradle's sdkmanager call itself retriable. Not possible.

Better robust approach: ask Gradle for the resolved ndkVersion and pre-install it:

```bash
cd flutter_app
NDK_VERSION=$(flutter --version ... )
```

Hmm. Actually, is there a simple command? `flutter config --list`? No. There is: `flutter doctor -v` prints "Android SDK at ... Android NDK at ..."? No, it doesn't print the required version.

Practical approach used by many projects: pin `ndkVersion` explicitly in `flutter_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts` to a concrete version (instead of `flutter.ndkVersion`), and pre-install it with `sdkmanager "ndk;VERSION" --licenses` with retry in the workflow. Pinning decouples Gradle config from Flutter's default bump, and the workflow pins the same version.

But hard-pinning ndkVersion in the app while flutter.ndkVersion bumps might cause a mismatch warning; AGP warns if ndkVersion missing but works with a pinned one. Flutter docs recommend setting ndkVersion explicitly in build.gradle — that's actually the Flutter-recommended practice for reproducible builds.

But wait — should I pin in app config or resolve at runtime in the workflow? Consider maintenance: when Flutter 3.48 bumps the default NDK, a hard-pinned app NDK stays 28.2.13676358 (fine, still installed via sdkmanager from workflow pin; the workflow pin and app pin must move together — two places).

Runtime resolution keeps a single source of truth (flutter.ndkVersion). How to resolve it in the workflow reliably? Grep the Flutter SDK gradle source:

In Flutter 3.47, the default ndkVersion lives in `packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt`:

```kotlin
val ndkVersion = "28.2.13676358" // or similar
```

Hmm, actually I recall `FlutterExtension.kt` has:

```kotlin
companion object {
    ...
    const val ndkVersion = "28.2.13676358"
}
```

I'm fairly sure the value lives there (it moved from flutter.groovy to FlutterExtension.kt). Let me check if Flutter SDK is available locally to verify. The environment has flutter? Let me check. If yes, I can grep locally and design a robust extraction.

Design decision — what's the minimal, convention-following fix?

Option A (follows gh-1468 precedent exactly): add a workflow step before `flutter build apk` that pre-installs the NDK with retry:

```yaml
# gh-1656: pre-install the Flutter-pinned NDK so Gradle config never
# triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build — a truncated
# download (gh-1655 CI red: "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%)
# is unretryable there and red'd the aggregate Quality gate. Same
# hardening as the flutter_gemma Android seed (gh-1468).
- name: Pre-install Android NDK (retry)
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    NDK_VERSION=...resolve...
    for attempt in 1 2 3; do
      if yes | sdkmanager --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then break; fi
      ...

name: flutter-gemma-android-seed
description: >-
  Pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android native cache so the
  flutter_gemma_litertlm build hook never downloads
  litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build. gh-1468: one HTTP 500 from the
  github.com release-asset CDN during that download red'd the ci.yml
  build-android leg (and the aggregate Quality gate with it). The hook
  short-circuits the download entirely once libLiteRtLm.so and a matching
  .flutter_gemma_native_version marker exist in the cache — same
  hardening the macOS legs carry via "Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion
  dylibs". The version/checksum below MUST equal the hook's _litertlmBundle
  registration in the pinned flutter_gemma_litertlm (hook/build.dart);
  test/ci_gemma_android_seed_guard_test.dart AC3 cross-checks both sides.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Seed flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/.cache/flutter_gemma/native"
        PLATFORM_DIR="$GEMMA_CACHE/android_arm64"
        MARKER="$GEMMA_CACHE/.flutter_gemma_native_version"
        # The hook's cache-dedup predicate: main lib present AND the
        # marker carries this bundle's exact version (its
        # _invalidateBundleCacheIfStale wipes owned files on a version
        # mismatch, so a stale seed would be deleted and re-downloaded
        # mid-build — the roulette this action exists to stop).
        if [ -f "$PLATFORM_DIR/libLiteRtLm.so" ] && \
           grep -q '"version":"0.17.1-a"\|"version": *"0.17.1-a"' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs already cached ($PLATFORM_DIR)"
        else
          echo "seeding flutter_gemma Android LiteRT-LM libs from native-v0.17.1-a"
          mkdir -p "$PLATFORM_DIR"
          curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
            -o /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.17.1-a/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz
          echo "745b89b606eb712a78f06aed41daca1370eae79b00e0a36054c8e775c0251768  /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz -C "$PLATFORM_DIR"
          # Marker commit point: {version, owner} exactly as the hook's
          # _writeMarker emits it (owner = the hook's _packageName) so the
          # pre-seeded cache keeps a single CodeAsset registrant.
          printf '{"version":"0.17.1-a","owner":"flutter_gemma_litertlm"}\n' > "$MARKER"
        fi
        ls -la "$PLATFORM_DIR"

build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON secret is not set — the Play Developer API service-account JSON key is required"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          echo "All required Android secrets are present"

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@e81a8fa391b11a595c1b7ed84177cc0fe02faf83 # v1.328.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # gh-1468: same seed as ci.yml build-android — the release lane runs
      # the same flutter_gemma_litertlm hook download and rides the same
      # release-asset CDN roulette without it.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      # The lane wraps `flutter build appbundle --release`; the upload
      # keystore rides the ANDROID_* env vars (issue #289) and is decoded
      # by app/build.gradle.kts into the (gitignored) build dir — no
      # key.properties dance. ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING makes a
      # secret-less release build fail LOUDLY instead of debug-signing.
      - name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          # gh-1522: the AAB's versionName rides the derived tag version
          # (BUILD_NAME) — the committed pubspec is the static 0.0.0-dev
          # placeholder and never churns. BUILD_NUMBER stays the run number
          # (Play versionCode).
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}

build-android-apks:
    # Issue #622: the flavor matrix. The AAB job above stays the Play
    # pipeline (store, unchanged); this job builds BOTH release APKs from
    # ONE variable — FLAVOR drives both the gradle --flavor and the
    # FA_FLAVOR dart-define (contract: the pair must never drift). god
    # (applicationId dev.fa1.app.god) is sideload-only and NEVER reaches
    # Play (binding threat model): it ships as an APK attached to the
    # GitHub release. store keeps its AAB for Play and additionally gets
    # an APK for direct installs + the UT-CI-1 size-delta tracking.
    name: Build Android APK (${{ matrix.flavor }})
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # Same placeholder-.env incantation as build-android (issue #368):
      # .env is a declared Flutter asset and newer flutter validates
      # assets at build time.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors build-android, gated to the store flavor: the secret file
      # carries ONLY the dev.fa1.app client, while the god applicationId is
      # dev.fa1.app.god — overwriting it would hard-fail the google-services
      # plugin ("No matching client found for package name
      # 'dev.fa1.app.god'"). god builds with the committed placeholder
      # google-services.json, which carries both clients.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ "$FLAVOR" != "store" ]; then
            echo "$FLAVOR builds with the committed placeholder google-services.json — the secret file has no dev.fa1.app.god client"
          elif [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written"
          else
            echo "GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      # runs the same flutter_gemma_litertlm hook download per leg.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      # with the SAME release key — only the applicationId differs), same
      # strict-signing posture: no silent debug-signed APKs. No Play
      # service account here — god never touches Play.
      - name: Build flavor APK

build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'

          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache on the

      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app

          set -euo pipefail

          BASE_URL=

      - name: Write placeholder GoogleService-Info.plist (Apple targets)
        if: matrix.target == 'ios' || matrix.target == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          BUNDLE_ID="dev.fa1.${{ matrix.target }}"
          GOOGLE_APP_ID="1:000000000000:${{ matrix.target }}:0000000000000000000000"
          cat > "flutter_app/${{ matrix.target }}/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist" << EOF
          <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
          <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">

I now have the complete picture. Design:

**Composite action** `.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall/action.yml`:
- composite, shell bash
- Resolves the NDK version the pinned Flutter SDK's gradle plugin declares (`val ndkVersion: String = "..."` in `$FLUTTER_ROOT/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt`) — the exact value `flutter.ndkVersion` resolves to, so version drift is impossible.
- Skips if `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties` exists (idempotent).
- Otherwise installs `ndk;$NDK_VERSION` via sdkmanager with up to 3 attempts (each attempt wipes any partial target dir).

Wait — one important check: in the failing run, Gradle invoked sdkmanager via `/usr/local/lib/android/sdk/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager`. `$ANDROID_HOME` on ubuntu runners = `/usr/local/lib/android/sdk`. sdkmanager must be on PATH or found at `$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager`. On ubuntu-latest images it's present. But hold on — do the Android licenses get accepted automatically? In the failing log, gradle triggered the NDK auto-install directly (no license prompt) — the image has licenses pre-accepted. Also build-ios leg uses the same image and it worked.

An extra robustness point: `yes | sdkmanager --licenses > /dev/null`? That would accept new licenses; but the image pre-accepts and the failing run shows gradle auto-installing without license issues. I'll include license acceptance guarded — actually keep it minimal and deterministic: only install; licenses are accepted on GitHub ubuntu-latest images (that's how the on-demand install inside Gradle succeeded 4 min later on main). Adding `--licenses` costs nothing though and covers runner-image license churn... I'll include it — cheap, idempotent, and consistent with "bounded retry" philosophy. Hmm, but it slows startup slightly (~2s). Fine.

Actually — one more design consideration: is sdkmanager even needed? Gradle auto-install IS sdkmanager under the hood; pre-installing via sdkmanager with retries is the natural fix.

Now the guard test `test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart`, following the gemma guard pattern:

- AC1: action exists, composite; body contains:
  - the FlutterExtension.kt resolution (single source of truth — assert it greps `ndkVersion` from `$FLUTTER_ROOT/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt`),
  - bounded retry (`for attempt in 1 2 3` or similar — assert `attempt` loop present),
  - idempotence skip (`ndk` dir check / `source.properties`),
  - fail-loud when the version cannot be resolved (`::error::` or clear failure) — a silent empty `ndk;` install would be worse.
- AC2: every Android-building job runs the action before its build step. Map (same as gemma guard):
  - ci.yml: build-android
  - build-mobile.yml: build-android, build-android-apks
  - nightly.yml: build-release
  Build signatures: `flutter build (apk|appbundle)`, `fastlane android build_release`, `matrix.cmd`.
  
  NOTE: nightly build-release is a matrix where `matrix.cmd` covers ALL targets (macos/ios/android/web/linux/windows) — the NDK action is only valid on ubuntu/android rows. The gemma seed handles this with `if: matrix.target == 'android'`. For the NDK action I'll also use `if: matrix.target == 'android'`. But then the guard's ordering check must tolerate the `if:` key. In the gemma guard, `step['uses'] == seedAction` works regardless of `if`. My guard mirrors that. Good.
- AC3: each workflow references the action exactly N times (1 for ci.yml, 2 for build-mobile.yml, 1 for nightly.yml).
- AC4 (env-dependent, named skip): if the local Flutter SDK's FlutterExtension.kt exists, the action's extraction regex matches it and the version matches `flutter.ndkVersion` — actually simpler: verify the regex in the action actually extracts a version from the local SDK file. This catches Flutter restructuring the gradle source (extraction breakage) — the kind of drift that would make the action fail. Named skip when `$FLUTTER_ROOT` (or common paths) missing.

For AC4 I need the exact extraction regex both in the action and the test to agree. Let me write it precisely:

Action:
```bash
GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_ROOT/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
```

Then fail loudly if empty:
```bash
if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
  echo "::error::cannot resolve the Flutter-pinned NDK version from $GRADLE_ROOT — Flutter's gradle plugin layout changed; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall"
  exit 1
fi
```

FLUTTER_ROOT fallback: `$FLUTTER_ROOT` is set by subosito/flutter-action (confirmed in job env). If unset, derive:
```bash
FLUTTER_ROOT="${FLUTTER_ROOT:-"$(cd "$(dirname "$(command -v flutter)")/.." && pwd)"}"
```

Idempotence:
```bash
if [ -f "$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
  echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping"
  exit 0
fi
```

Retry loop:
```bash
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
  rm -rf "$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
  if yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION" > /tmp/ndk-install.log 2>&1; then

    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
  tail -5 /tmp/ndk-install.log || true

done
echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655: a mid-download truncated NDK archive ('Error on ZipFile unknown archive') red'd the build-android leg and the aggregate Quality gate; see /tmp/ndk-install.log"
exit 1
```

SDKMANAGER resolution:
```bash
SDKMANAGER="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
[ -x "$SDKMANAGER" ] || SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ] || [ ! -e "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then ... error; fi
```

Yes, standard behavior: AGP looks up NDK at `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version>` (auto-install also lands there via sdkmanager). Once present, no download.

And the android matrix row of nightly's build-release — pinned 3.47.x, ubuntu. Good.

blocks.text:
No special config for the gemma guard test — it's just a regular test file in `test/`. Good, my new guard test follows the same placement.

Now let me write the guard test first (RED). I'll model it closely on the gemma guard.

Key content assertions for the action (AC1):
1. `.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall/action.yml` exists, `using: composite`.
2. Resolves the version from the Flutter SDK gradle plugin source — assert the body references `packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt` and extracts `val ndkVersion`.
3. Fails loudly when unresolved (`::error::`).
4. Idempotent skip when installed (`source.properties`).
5. Bounded retry: 3 attempts (`attempt in 1 2 3` / `attempt/3`).
6. Installs via sdkmanager `ndk;$NDK_VERSION` into `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/...` — AGP's lookup path.
7. A local-SDK cross-check (AC4): if the local Flutter SDK file exists, the action's extraction pattern must match it — this is where I validate the regex actually extracts `28.2.13676358` from the real SDK (env-dependent, named skip). This is my "reproduces the drift class" test.

For AC2 I mirror the gemma guard's androidBuildJobs map and build signatures.

AC3: exact reference counts per workflow.

Now write the test. One thing to be careful about: the `if:`-guarded step in nightly — `step['uses']` still matches.

Also the gemma guard asserts build-signature matching `run:` strings: in build-mobile.yml line 245, `bundle exec fastlane android build_release` — matches `fastlane android build_release\b`. Line 468: `flutter build apk --release ...` matches. ci.yml 2494 matches. nightly: `matrix.cmd` signature.

For the ordering check: my action step (`uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall`) must appear BEFORE each build index. In build-mobile.yml, the build steps are `run:` blocks — fine.

Let me now write the test file.

For the retry-loop assertion, pin the exact strings:
- `contains('--install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"')`
- retry: `contains('for attempt in 1 2 3')` and `contains('attempt 2/3')`? Simpler: assert `for attempt in 1 2 3` and a `sleep` between attempts, plus fail-loud `::error::` after exhausting attempts.
- idempotence: `contains('source.properties')`.
- SDK path: `contains('cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager')`.
- extraction: `contains('FlutterExtension.kt')` and `contains('val ndkVersion')`.

And AC4: replicate the extraction locally:
```dart
final sdkCandidates = [
  Platform.environment['FLUTTER_ROOT'],
  '/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter/stable-3.47.7-x64/flutter',
  ...
];
```
Hmm — hardcoding the hostedtoolcache path is env-specific and would fail elsewhere... The gemma guard's AC3 pattern: derive candidates from env with a named skip if absent. In THIS environment `/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter/stable-3.47.7-x64/flutter` exists. Better to check env FLUTTER_ROOT first, then glob `/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter/*/flutter`? That's a reasonable generic pattern for this runner. If nothing found → named skip (print + return), exactly like the gemma guard's AC3 fallback. If found → assert the extraction finds `val ndkVersion: String = "28.2.13676358"` AND that the action's declared extraction regex matches the same line. Since the action's regex is embedded in a bash string, simplest robust cross-check: extract with the same regex the action uses (duplicated in the test as a constant) against the local SDK file and assert non-null. The value itself I shouldn't pin (Flutter bumps would churn the test)... but pinning is what the gemma guard does for drift-coupling. For NDK, the value is resolved at runtime from the SDK — no pin to keep in sync — so the test asserts "extraction succeeds against the real SDK", which is the actual risk (Flutter restructuring the Kotlin file). I'll also assert the extracted version parses as `\d+\.\d+\.\d+`.

Wait, actually — should the test ALSO assert the gradle side (`flutter_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts` uses `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion` — i.e. the app tracks the SDK's value, so runtime resolution from the SDK can never skew)? Yes! That's a valuable coupling assertion: if someone pins a literal ndkVersion in app/build.gradle.kts, the action's runtime-resolved value could skew from what AGP requests. Assert `contains('ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion')`. If a future change pins a literal there, this test forces a conscious update of the action/test.

Now the action itself. Let me write it carefully.

```yaml
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated NDK download ("Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%) red'd
  the ci.yml build-android leg and the aggregate Quality gate with it;
  Gradle's own auto-install path has no retry. The NDK version is resolved
  from the pinned Flutter SDK's gradle plugin source (the exact value
  flutter.ndkVersion resolves to — no second pin to drift), the install is
  skipped when the NDK is already present, and the download itself is
  bounded-retried — the same hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed
  carries (gh-1468).
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at config
        # time (a literal pin on either side would break that coupling —
        # the ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test pins both sides).
        FLUTTER_HOME="${FLUTTER_ROOT:-$(dirname "$(dirname "$(command -v flutter)")}"
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall"
          exit 1
        fi
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager)"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call, run
